newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close higher in technical correction.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close higher in technical correction.

text.p: FCOJ futures reversed course after three consecutive days of losses and closed firmer in a temporary consolidation, market sources said.
But the overall trend remains lower with nearby support pegged at the 1993 low of 65.45 cents followed by 60.00 cents.
September juice ended 1.85 cents higher at 69.05 cents a lb, having ranged from 69.50 to 67.60 cents. The rest of the board settled 1.70 to 0.95 firmer.
Trade buying buoyed prices amid a dearth of selling but the benchmark September contract failed to reach its upside target of 70.00 cents, the high hit on Monday.
Analysts said record orange production in both Florida and Brazil will keep the market under pressure, particularly since demand remains flat and U.S. retail prices high.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture will issue its first estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop in October. A private forecast last week pegged the crop at a record 253 million 90-lb boxes, 12 percent higher than the 225.7 million boxes produced in 1996/97.
Open interest in the September contract fell 1,417 lots as of Monday while open interest in the market rose by 579 lots.
Players expect the NYCE weekly spec/hedge report on Wednesday to reveal that the speculators have slightly decreased their 77.7 percent long position in the market.
An estimated 8,500 lots changed hands on the day compared with Monday's official 11,125 lots.
